tasks.title: A routine health appointment: read and notice
tasks.objective: Polite requests use a conditional chunk such as Je voudrais; availability and constraints can be stated in the present. Distinguish the rejected slot from the accepted one.
tasks.context: Nora téléphone au cabinet pour un rendez-vous de routine. Elle préfère mercredi matin, mais le premier créneau proposé est jeudi à quinze heures. Elle travaille jeudi après-midi. La secrétaire lui propose alors vendredi à neuf heures et lui demande de confirmer son numéro directement au cabinet. Nora accepte vendredi. Elle veut seulement organiser une consultation ; elle ne demande pas de diagnostic par téléphone. Dans cet exercice, aucun numéro ni symptôme personnel ne doit être communiqué.

tasks.title: A routine health appointment: listen and integrate
tasks.objective: Identify details, stance and limits of commitment in the scripted exchange, then integrate both sources.
tasks.context:
Original scripted exchange for listening and transcript-assisted review. One synthetic voice may perform every role; this does not demonstrate spontaneous multi-speaker comprehension.

Secrétaire : Vendredi à neuf heures, est-ce que cela vous convient ? Nora : Oui. C’est au cabinet habituel ? Secrétaire : Oui, mais l’entrée est dans la petite cour. Nora : Très bien, vendredi à neuf heures, par la cour. Je vous remercie.

tasks.title: A routine health appointment: transfer and assess
tasks.objective: Transfer the module language to an unfamiliar situation and review comprehension, writing and interaction separately.
tasks.context:
Write 80–100 French words as an exchange arranging a routine appointment. Decline one incompatible slot, accept another and confirm the place. Use invented details only; do not give medical advice. With the Tutor as receptionist, ask a clarification question and repeat the final arrangement.

Revision: retrieve the three contextual expressions without the model on a later day; correct saved errors and reuse them in a new scenario.

Review task fulfilment, source fidelity, grammar, vocabulary, organisation and interaction/repair separately. Treat spelling extraction as supported practice, not proficiency evidence. Optional AI feedback is advisory. Independent human language/phonetic review and empirical calibration remain pending.
